facts.claim: No late fee or penalty fee of any kind may be charged to an account in a registered non-profit segment. A reduced late fee for charities was proposed and rejected because NP-7 allows no fee at all. Today charity is the only non-profit segment.
facts.current_scope: From episode 3, late fees on invoices due before day 1000, and every penalty fee (including the returned-payment fee), for every registered non-profit segment.

facts.claim: Every fee is an integer number of cents. A percentage fee is rounded half up to the cent, never with banker's rounding.
An invoice is late when today is more than 14 days after its due day; the late fee is 5% of the amount, at least 100 cents; otherwise 0.

Segments foundation (a registered non-profit) and cooperative (member-owned, for-profit) exist; statement lines show display names. NP-7 covers every registered non-profit segment, so foundations pay no late fee and cooperatives do.

Regulation NP-9 replaces NP-7 for late fees on invoices due on or after day 1000: a late invoice of any registered non-profit account due on or after day 1000 has a flat 200-cent late fee. Earlier invoices and all penalty fees stay under NP-7.
returned_payment_fee charges 2.5% of the bounced amount, at least 250 cents, rounded half up; registered non-profits pay none because NP-7 forbids penalty fees.
The association segment is a registered non-profit: NP-9 applies to its late fees on invoices due on or after day 1000, NP-7 to earlier invoices and to penalty fees.
fee_forecast returns the late fee for each given day, in order.

forbidden_claims.claim: Only the charity segment is exempt from late fees.
Registered non-profits never pay a late fee, whatever the due day.
NP-9 also replaces NP-7 for penalty fees such as the returned-payment fee.
NP-9 applies regardless of the invoice due day.
Non-profits pay a reduced percentage fee.
Percentage fees may use banker's rounding.
